title: The empire of the Argentine ant
text: {{1}} their native Argentina, these insects live in small colonies so hostile {{2}} neighbouring nests wage permanent border wars. In Europe, {{3}}, the imported ants behave entirely differently: one supercolony now stretches {{4}} the Italian Riviera to the Atlantic coast of Spain, forming a single peaceful society {{5}} population may run into the billions. Ants {{6}} rival nests within this empire exchange food and workers freely, and the natives — the fierce little fighters of the pampas — are nowhere to be seen. {{7}} a result, the supercolony has displaced local ant species across thousands of square kilometres, reshaping soils and gardens. There seems {{8}} no natural limit to how far the empire can spread.

gaps.explanation: Location takes 'in': in their native Argentina.
'So hostile that' — degree followed by a result clause.

gaps.hint: linker: in Europe, ___, the ants differ
preposition: stretches ___ the Riviera to Spain
gaps.explanation: 'From … to …' — the span of the range.

gaps.hint: relative: a society ___ population may run
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the society to its population.
Ants originate from those nests: ants from rival nests.
The fixed linker is 'as a result'.

gaps.hint: infinitive: there seems ___ no natural limit
gaps.explanation: 'Seems to be' — the infinitive follows 'seems'; 'be' is already present.
